text:
maria: Heads-up — I ran the spline bucketing run over the latest traffic sample (1h) to see if prompt-rate bucketing helps the continuous batcher pick better kernels. Results below, tl;dr: some improvement on 8k-long tails but KV thrash increased for mid-lengths.

devin: good, can you paste the config you used?

maria: sure — small snippet: 
```
queue_policy: 
  type: continuous
  bucket_scheme: spline
  spline_knots: [16, 64, 256, 1024, 4096]
  token_budget_targets: [64, 128, 256, 512, 1024]
  decode_rate_buckets: dynamic
```

lia: interesting — spline_knots spacing looks aggressive at the high end. Did you try smoothing the token budgets?

maria: i did a pass with a 0.8 smoothing factor on budgets, reduced KV evictions by ~12% for 512–2048 prompt lengths. Raw profiling: 

perf-bot: Kernel selection summary:
  - selected cuda_fused_attn for <256 tokens (70% of requests)
  - aten_attention for 256–1024 (20%)
  - fallback int8_host for >1024 (10%)

maria: decode rate observations: top-heavy tail at ~120 tok/s for streaming clients; spline buckets moved some long prompts into larger token_budget but that pushed KV cache working set up -> more cross-tenant evictions on Dedicated32.

sam: any regression on p95 latency?

maria: p95 for small (<256) unchanged at 68ms. p95 for 256–1024 went from 240ms -> 275ms (regression) while >1024 improved from 980ms -> 880ms. So tradeoff.

devin: sounds like kernel handoff boundaries need shifting. Maybe split 256–1024 into two buckets at 512 and prefer fused kernels up to 512. Also consider a per-worker KV budget cap to avoid cross-tenant thrash.

lia: +1. Also, can we feed decode_rate into the classifier? If a request is high tok/s we bias towards faster kernels even if length suggests otherwise.

maria: tested a quick heuristic: if decode_rate > 90 tok/s, bump token_budget target by 1 bucket. Reduced p95 regression by half for 256–512. I can push the probe patch.

sam: post the perf run and the flamegraphs when you have them. can we also add an admission rule to avoid mixing >4096 and <256 in same microbatch?

maria: yes — added soft demux rule in queue_policy to prefer homogeneous microbatches; that cut KV evictions another ~8%. I'll upload the run artifacts to the perf bucket.

devin: nice. after artifacts, let's schedule a quick canary on dedicated-alpha tomorrow. i'll coordinate with infra. @lia can you review the kernel-handoff thresholds?

lia: on it. quick note — the spline approach looks promising for long-tail optimization, but we should not overfit to the 1h sample. need a week-long run with mixed traffic.

maria: agreed. will schedule longer run with traffic replay and include a step that logs KV eviction reasons and kernel-change events.

perf-bot: Run uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/1748509123/spline-buckets/run-1.tar.gz :thumbsup:

sam: great. tagging this thread for follow-up: we'll reconvene after the week-long run. :calendar:
